steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: How have you been, Chief ${PlayerName}?
She deliberately enunciates your name in a not so friendly way.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Thanks to you, my patients and colleagues are dead, my hospital has been blown up, and now...

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: You've confined me to this interrogation room. What do you want?
The harsh lighting doesn't deter Iron at all. She glares at you from across the table with piercing gaze.
With such hostility, it will probably be hard to convince her to work with the FAC.

options: Put on relaxed airs & cozy up to her

choices.text: Put on relaxed airs & cozy up to her

steps.content: We're no strangers to each other. You can relax a bit.
Back at SALVA, we were even comrades-in-arms...

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Ha, comrades-in-arms?
She cuts you off with a cold chuckle.
I'm deeply sorry for what happened at SALVA. I know you won't be able to talk to me calmly anytime soon.
But as you saw, I harbor no ill intentions toward Sinners. You don't need to be so guarded against me. We have the same goal.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Ha, the same...
She cuts you off with a cold chuckle.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: SALVA sacrificed lives to save Syndicate. How can it be the same?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Now, Chief of Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, there are two things you need to be clear about.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: First, I am innocent. Everything I've done is to heal Syndicate.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Put away your interrogation tactics. I don't care for them. No matter what evidence you have, I will not kowtow to authority.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Second...
She gazes at you with a tiny trace of gloom in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Second, I'm not your comrade-in-arms, let alone your friend.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: We both know how much damage your presence has dealt to the hospital.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: You want me to put on a smile and chat with you like nothing ever happened? And in this tapped interrogation room full of surveillance equipment, of all places? Ha...

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Dream on.
She clearly has no more patience to humor you after saying this. Her mechanical left hand clenches and unclenches impatiently.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: If you get what I mean, then stop wasting time. Now tell me, what do those cowards want from me?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Pfff... the FAC, that organization who's supposed to exist for the sole purpose of controlling Mania.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: And yet, they sent a clueless Chief and two little girls to Syndicate when the Mania crisis is at its peak.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Though all you could do was to hide behind the Sinners, at least your shackles and decisions played a crucial role. But as for them...

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: All the disorder and evil in Syndicate nowadays, they're inextricably linked to the FAC's incompetence and dereliction of duty. Can you blame me for calling them cowards?

options: Fair enough. I've heard worse curses in Syndicate...
How do you know I'm sent by the FAC?

choices.text: Fair enough. I've heard worse curses in Syndicate...
How do you know I'm sent by the FAC?

steps.content: You don't know how Nightingale will react if you talk about FAC's noble deeds under close surveillance, but for the sake of the negotiations, you have no choice but to continue the topic.
But how did you know it has to do with the FAC?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: An educated guess.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Back at SALVA, you saw my surgical experiments. Your reaction at the time was interesting.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: My observations of you tell me that the authorities have not yet grasped how to surgically suppress Mania.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Surely they won't ignore the mountain of patient data SALVA retrieved from Syndicate, as well as over a hundred clinical records I made.
But you just said FAC was incompetent in the face of Mania. How can you be sure that they want to know about your surgeries?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: ...Because of you.
Iron's tone softens noticeably.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I can tell that you want to save lives, regardless of gender or age, or whether they're civilians, Maniacs or Sinners.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: It's true that I'm not sure what the FAC wants, but as for you... I know for sure that you won't give up on treating Mania. You'll definitely push for military-civilian cooperation.

As she had guessed, you listed in detail what you saw and heard at SALVA in the Syndicate mission report, and refuted rumors about horrific experiments taking place there. You hope that SALVA's good deeds in Syndicate can be taken seriously by the FAC.
But Iron got one thing wrong.
test
test
test
test
test
test

I did report the contributions made by you and SALVA towards fighting Mania to my superiors, but this cooperation isn't pushed by me. The FAC issued an order before I could draft a cooperation proposal.
My report piqued their interest, and they hope to collaborate with you on Mania research and find a cure.
Her brows twitch as she carefully examines the order document on the table, but she remains silent.
The wait for her reply is torturous. After what seemed like an eternity, she finally lifts her head.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I refuse.
Why?
Iron's decision seems incomprehensible. The FAC can provide her with personnel, technical and limitless financial support, yet she still chooses to reject the offer after careful consideration.
Sensing your confusion, she smiles and pushes the document back to you.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Compared to a few empty promises on paper, I'm more inclined to trust what I saw in Syndicate with my own eyes.

options: You still don't trust the FAC

choices.text: You still don't trust the FAC

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: What has the FAC ever been responsible for that merits any trust? The gang wars? The proliferation of Mania weapons? Or... the patients on my operating table that they've neglected and abandoned?
Her sudden sharp questions leave you speechless.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Ha, forget it. I thank them for their kind offer, but I refuse to cooperate until I see some sincerity from the FAC.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Even without funding, technology, or even a clinic, I will continue the Mania research on my own.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Even if I'm the only one left...
Iron speaks in an extra grave tone as she frowns at her left arm. It seems that she is trying to convince herself more so than you.
Perhaps you already know why she's frowning...
But can you really continue only on your own?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: What do you mean? Are you doubting my medical skills now?
No, I'm doubting how well a doctor can treat an illness when she is seriously ill herself.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
According to the tests taken at the time of your detainment, your base M-value is higher than most other Sinners.
As a professional researcher of Mania, you know better than I do what this means.
Iron does not respond. She just stares at the file data in cold silence, so you continue the topic yourself.

This means that when you awakened as a Sinner, your M-value was already so high that you were on the brink of derangement. Each time your M-value increases, you get one step closer to becoming a Corruptor.
If the mutation really occurs, you won't even be able to save yourself with your sanity lost, let alone save Syndicate.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: There are no what-ifs. Your shackles are the best bet for suppressing Mania.
The shackles won't last forever. If something happens to me...

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I told you, there are no what-ifs!
Your words enrage Iron for some reason. Her mechanical left arm slaps against the armrest of the interrogation chair, making shrill noises.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: For your information, I already told Anne before I met you that I'd operate on myself before I mutate.

options: You'll perform nerve modification surgery on yourself?

choices.text: You'll perform nerve modification surgery on yourself?

steps.content: Then you'll become like Ted. You'll lose all desires and become a walking corpse...

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: What I become has nothing to do with you!

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: But your shackles are critical to the M-value of every Sinner in the Bureau. It's the unsolved enigma to restraining Mania, and the hope of DisCity!

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I won't let these what-ifs come true.
Those are supposed to be words showing concern, but she manages to make them sound harsh and menacing.

options: I promise you, I won't die easily
I'm sorry, I shouldn't have joked about such things

choices.text: I promise you, I won't die easily
I'm sorry, I shouldn't have joked about such things

steps.content: You take back your assumptions, and Iron's rage cools a bit.
Yet as you observe Iron fuming, you can't help but remember that iron-blooded devil standing before the ruins of SALVA.
Irritability is a Mania symptom, and it is still affecting her life.
My shackles can indeed prevent you from mutating, but what about the nightmares, insomnia, the mental and emotional anguish? What about the searing sores on your body...
You look at Iron's left shoulder, where her robotic arm connects to her torso. According to the physical examination, there had been severe ulcerations there.
What Sinners with high M-value are suffering from is a hundred times worse than what has been recorded on paper.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: Pain, insomnia, and irritability can all be controlled with medication.
Long-term use of such medication will definitely lead to dependence and resistance, which can only be restrained by taking more medication. There is no end to such treatment.
She caresses her left arm, pretending to not care.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I'm a medical professional. I know what dosage to use. No need for you to worry about it.

options: You are as ruthless to yourself as you are to the patients

choices.text: You are as ruthless to yourself as you are to the patients

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: ...I'm not trying to be ruthless.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: It's a choice that must be made to heal Syndicate.
She has left herself no room to back out.
By this point, it doesn't seem like anything new will come from the interrogation. You two just sit face-to-face in silence across the FAC files and medical reports. She's waiting for you to talk.

options: That's it for the interrogation today.
So you are still not willing to cooperate with the FAC?

choices.text: That's it for the interrogation today.
So you are still not willing to cooperate with the FAC?

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: You still haven't completed the mission your superiors assigned you.
You said that you refuse to cooperate until you see some sincerity from the FAC.
I'll make sure you see some.
She smiles, finally relaxing a bit.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I can do it on my own.
I will let you see the FAC's sincerity.
She smiles, finally relaxing a bit, noncommittal at your answer.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: All the nurses at SALVA call me stubborn behind my back. No one can sway my decisions. But this time...
She flashes her eyebrows half-jokingly.

steps.speaker: Iron
steps.content: I seem to have met my match.
